chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The fasting of the month of Patience (Ramadan) and three days in every month remove the evil thoughts from the chests.
And the fasting of three days in every month is the fasting of the entire life.
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: 'Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have ten like it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.بَلَابِلُ الصُّدُورِ: Evil thoughts or whispers in the chest/heart
key_terms.شَهْرِ الصَّبْرِ: The month of Patience, referring to Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of fasting three days each month in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that fasting during Ramadan and fasting three days each month purges the heart of evil thoughts. These three days are considered equivalent to fasting for a lifetime because of the multiplier of good deeds, as cited from the Quranic verse stating that one good deed is rewarded tenfold. In Shia tradition, this specific triad of days—often identified as the first Thursday, middle Wednesday, and last Thursday—serves as a spiritual purification mechanism, linking the cosmic significance of lunar phases with the internal cleansing of the soul.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates that Amirul Momineen (a.s.) said, “The fasts of the month of Patience (Ramadan) and three fasts of a month keep the evil-thoughts away from one’s heart.
The three fasts of a month are equal to the fasts of  an  age
for  Allah  says  in  His  book,  “Whoever  brings  a good deed, he shall have ten like it.”9
